solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drake maybe very quiet in turning back

indicators.note: the musical very-quiet marking is placed in the middle of the other piece
turning signals that the word for back is read the other way round

parts.note: the back of something is its rear
PP, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: A duck, perhaps, slips silently round behind something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses the word for back and 'in' sets the musical marking inside. Drake is a Canadian hip-hop star, not a male duck here.
explanation.definitionFit: Drake is a well-known hip-hop musician, so he is an example of one who raps.

clue.text: Last of all, engineers weapons taking over third of nation

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps

indicators.note: the weapons word takes in, or holds, the cricket abbreviation

parts.note: weapons are arms
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: third of means the third letter of the word nation is picked out

explanation.surface: Finally, military engineers arm themselves and seize part of a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' puts O inside ARMS to make ARMOS; 'third of' picks T from nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed at the very back of a line, furthest behind all others, is last of all.

clue.text: Asian king is drawn in by smashing pinata

indicators.note: the king and is are drawn into the middle of the rearranged party-toy letters
a smashed pinata is broken up, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch from Asia is pulled in by a pinata being broken at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' signals the anagram and 'drawn in by' sets the king and 'is' within the scrambled letters, splitting them after the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from a country in South Asia is an Asian, so the nationality fits the broader term.

clue.text: English member and soldier is debonair

parts.note: a limb such as a leg is a member of the body
a soldier ant is a kind of ant, so ant stands for soldier in crosswords

explanation.surface: An English club member who was once a soldier is suave.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair and the answer are synonyms, both describing someone stylish, refined and graceful in manner.

clue.text: Spinning good election?

parts.note: PI is informal for pious, that is good or holy
an election is a process of voting

explanation.surface: A wry question whether a ballot that has been spun can count as good.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is a crossword staple for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning round on an axis or point is spinning, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Error in entry about corrupt nature

indicators.note: about says the word for entry goes around the scrambled letters

parts.note: access is a way in, an entry

indicators.note: corrupt suggests something spoilt or altered, so the letters of nature are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mistake in a record about human nature turning bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' gives URATEN, and 'about' wraps the entry word around those letters, after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Incorrectness or imprecision is a state of error, so the long noun is a synonym.

clue.text: Folding money initially pressed by old equipment — excellent!

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment

indicators.note: the initial letter of money is pressed between the letters of the excellent word

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written with I for the figure 1

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of money

explanation.surface: Paper money pressed flat by some antique kit: wonderful!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Folding money' looks like one phrase meaning banknotes, but Folding is the definition. 'pressed by' puts M inside AI (A1).
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese craft of shaping paper into figures by creasing it is the art of folding.

clue.text: Island queen, queen for northern Arab

indicators.note: for here means one letter is swapped in place of another

parts.note: a rani is a Hindu queen
Q is the chess abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: An island monarch, then another queen, standing in for a northern Arab.
explanation.walkthrough: I + RANI gives IRANI, an Iranian; 'for' swaps its N for Q.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Baghdad's country is an Arab, the nation being part of the Arab world.

clue.text: Going round hospital, arrive at poor district

indicators.note: the phrase for arriving goes round the hospital letter

parts.note: to arrive at a place is to get to it

explanation.surface: On a round of the hospital, someone reaches a deprived neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going round' puts H inside GET TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A deprived, densely populated quarter of a city, often home to a minority, is a poor district.

clue.text: Image software provides ways to enjoy view

parts.note: an image is a picture
Windows is Microsoft's operating system software

explanation.surface: A computer screen's image and operating system offer a nice outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Large single panes of glass that frame a landscape are ways for people indoors to take in the scenery.

clue.text: Joint stank less internally

indicators.note: internally says the letters sit inside the phrase stank less

explanation.surface: A sore joint smelled less inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The part where the foot meets the leg is a hinge in the body, a joint.

clue.text: Maintain criminal facing life, ultimately, is dead

indicators.note: criminal means wrong or bad, so the letters of maintain are disordered
ultimately picks the final letter of life

explanation.surface: A villain who insists his life is basically over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' turns MAINTAIN into INANIMAT; 'ultimately' adds E from life.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifeless and without animation, an object that never lived or no longer does can be called dead.

clue.text: Is M apparently put in the wrong film?

parts.note: split the solution 3,4: MIS with the anagram signal cast after it gives the scrambled letters IS M

explanation.surface: Could James Bond's spy boss be played by the wrong actor?
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: read the answer as wordplay, 'MIS cast' (thrown about), and you get IS M. M is James Bond's boss, which makes the casting surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To give an actor an unsuitable role is to cast them badly, putting them in the wrong film.

clue.text: Zulu entering estate maybe is threatening at first for despotic supporter

indicators.note: the Zulu letter enters the vehicle word

parts.note: an estate is a type of car, so car is suggested by example
Z is Zulu in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: at first picks the first letter of threatening

explanation.surface: A Zulu warrior bursts onto a country estate, menacing, in support of a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British name for a station wagon. 'entering' puts Z in CAR; 'at first' gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Russian emperors' autocratic rule is a backer of a despot.

clue.text: Careless bird nears cat, mad about tea mostly

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters go round the shortened drink
mad suggests wild disorder, so the letters of bird nears cat are jumbled
mostly means the word tea loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A dizzy bird wanders up to a cat, going crazy over a cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' signals the anagram, 'about' puts the scrambled letters around the drink, and 'mostly' cuts the last letter from tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A flighty, forgetful person is careless, lacking attention or thought.

clue.text: Lunatic gets eager for festival food

indicators.note: lunatic means crazy, so the letters of gets eager are scrambled

explanation.surface: A madman becomes keen on holiday treats.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate treat given at the spring Christian feast is a food tied to a festival.

clue.text: Start of Jane Eyre, oddly, with lines about new repository of refined output

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of Jane
oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of Eyre

parts.note: RY, railway, means lines
CA, circa, means about

explanation.surface: The opening of Jane Eyre, read oddly, with some lines about a novel kind of storage.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'refined output' is fuel from an oil refinery, and the answer is a petrol can.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-sided metal fuel can holds petrol, the product of an oil refinery.

clue.text: Alcohol and tea cocktail? Novel!

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic drink
with means along with, and
Rosie Lee is Cockney rhyming slang for tea, shortened to Rosie

explanation.surface: A mix of booze and tea: what a new idea!
explanation.walkthrough: Rosie Lee rhymes with tea in Cockney rhyming slang. The answer is Laurie Lee's 1959 memoir of a Cotswold childhood.
explanation.definitionFit: The book by Laurie Lee is a famous English work of fiction-like memoir, here called a novel.

clue.text: Inspect base under old dictator?

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means the base comes after the rest

parts.note: ex means former, or old
Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda
E is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: Look closely at the foundations underneath a former tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: To look over something carefully is to inspect it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Meet in harbour

definitions.meaning: to meet guests is to greet and welcome them
to harbour something is to take it in and hold it, as stolen goods

explanation.surface: Two verbs joined by a link: greet guests and also shelter them.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are fulfilled: you welcome guests, and you accept and keep goods such as stolen property.

clue.text: Fake empty yarn about Tom?

indicators.note: empty means the inside letters of fake are removed, keeping only its ends

parts.note: a line can mean a yarn or thread

explanation.surface: A wild made-up story about a cat called Tom.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom is a male cat, so the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomcat is a male cat, so it is a member of the cat family.

clue.text: Defend student in former trouble

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the student letter goes in the trouble word

parts.note: pain can mean trouble or bother
L, for learner, stands for a student

explanation.surface: Stand up for a pupil who was once in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner-driver plate letter, a crossword stand-in for student.
explanation.definitionFit: To justify or account for an action is to defend it with reasons.

clue.text: Youngster takes work, producing annoying advert

indicators.note: the youngster word takes in the work word

parts.note: a pup is a young animal, a youngster
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A young person gets a job and makes an irritating commercial.
explanation.definitionFit: A window that suddenly appears over a web page selling something is an irritating online ad.

clue.text: With nitrogen displaced, vague about what's at the core

indicators.note: displaced means the nitrogen letter is taken from its place and set somewhere else

parts.note: vague means unclear
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Chemistry talk about shifting nitrogen and being unsure of the central matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displaced' moves the N of UNCLEAR to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a nucleus, the central part of an atom or cell, means concerning its core.

clue.text: Confines devil with prayers, nothing's lost

parts.note: an imp is a little devil

indicators.note: lost means the nothing letter is dropped from the prayers word

parts.note: orisons are prayers
O, zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A demon with lost prayers, all dashed, locks someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes O from ORISONS to give RISONS.
explanation.definitionFit: To lock someone up in jail is to confine them, so the verb forms match.

clue.text: Intestinal bile actor is repressing

indicators.note: the phrase bile actor holds down, or keeps inside it, the letters needed

explanation.surface: An actor with digestive trouble is holding back his bile.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the ileum, part of the small intestine, so it is an intestinal word.

clue.text: Oil company drops Trump, perhaps, in drink

indicators.note: the oil company drops the president in, so that abbreviation goes inside the company name

parts.note: Esso is a trading name of the oil firm that began as Standard Oil
Trump was a president, abbreviated pres

explanation.surface: An oil firm sacks the US president over a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' looks like sacking Trump, but 'drops ... in' means lets the president fall inside the company name.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong, concentrated coffee made by forcing steam through grounds is a drink.

clue.text: Former leader at first raw, excitable and good at nothing?

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of each of the next six words

explanation.surface: An ex-leader starting out green and jumpy, but useless?
explanation.definitionFit: The former film actor was a US president in the 1980s, a past leader.
